findings.title: Immortal time bias and prevalent user design
findings.mechanism: Defining exposure as any prior or current prescription without requiring a new-user design, active comparator, or time-to-event analysis creates immortal time where exposed patients had to survive and remain cancer-free until GLP-1 initiation to be classified as exposed.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio below 1.0 (spuriously protective for GLP-1), as demonstrated by the lower event rate in the GLP-1 group (1.62% vs 2.47% full, 1.62% vs 2.31% matched).
evidence: Exposure defined as 'любое prior или current использование'
No washout period or minimum treatment duration
Logistic regression used instead of time-to-event analysis

findings.title: Selection bias via conditioning on mammography screening
findings.mechanism: The entire cohort was selected exclusively from patients who underwent screening mammography (217,624 initial pool), while screening frequency was explicitly not balanced between arms. Differential healthcare engagement and screening behavior between GLP-1 users and controls directly affects detection probability.
findings.direction: Could bias in either direction, but given that screening frequency was unadjusted and controls have a higher event rate (2.31% vs 1.62%), controls may have had higher cumulative screening or surveillance intensity.

findings.title: Residual confounding and reverse causality (protopathic bias / contraindication)
findings.mechanism: History of prior breast cancer and general comorbidity were not matched. Physicians avoid prescribing GLP-1 receptor agonists to patients with active malignancies, cachexia, or severe multimorbidity, channelling patients with existing or incipient cancer into the control arm. Furthermore, a 3.5-year observation window is insufficient for true chemopreventive tumor initiation/progression reduction.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio below 1.0 (falsely favoring GLP-1) by concentrating undiagnosed or historical cancer cases in the control group (353 vs 247 events in matched cohort).

findings.title: Prevalent user and immortal time bias in exposure definition
findings.mechanism: Defining exposure as any prior or current prescription before the cutoff without a new-user design, washout period, or minimum duration requirement allows immortal person-time prior to the first prescription to be misattributed and preferentially selects survivors/tolerant long-term users.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio downwards (toward a false protective effect), because surviving long enough to receive a prescription or remaining on therapy without an adverse diagnosis inherently selects for lower event rates.
evidence: Exposure definition: Any prior or current use; first prescription before cut-off date
No minimum duration required
No washout period applied
Time-to-event analysis was not conducted

findings.title: Uncontrolled confounding by prior cancer history and lack of exclusion criteria
findings.mechanism: Patients with prior breast cancer were not excluded from the cohort and matching did not balance prior breast cancer history. Mixing prevalent/recurrent cancer cases with incident cancer without time-to-event tracking distorts true incidence.

findings.title: Unaccounted competing risk of mortality and severe comorbidity imbalance
findings.mechanism: GLP-1 users have roughly double the burden of severe comorbidity, cardiovascular disease, and renal disease. In a standard logistic regression without time-to-event or competing risk modeling, sicker patients are at higher risk of dying or dropping out before screening/diagnosis of breast cancer occurs during the short window.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio downwards (falsely protective), as GLP-1 users are more likely to experience competing mortality or clinical triage away from routine cancer detection.

findings.title: Biologically implausible latency within a restricted observation window
findings.mechanism: The observation window is only 3.5 years (Jan 2022 to Jun 2025). Carcinogenesis and solid tumor risk reduction operate on long multi-year to decadal latencies; an observed 30-35% reduction in solid tumor incidence within 3.5 years without lag periods reflects protopathic/detection dynamics rather than biological chemoprevention.
findings.direction: Pushes the odds ratio downwards (spurious rapid protective effect).

findings.title: Immortal Time Bias
findings.mechanism: The study uses logistic regression over a 3.5-year follow-up period, which improperly handles time. Patients in the GLP-1 group are only considered 'exposed' after their first prescription. The time between the study start and their first prescription is 'immortal time'—a period where they cannot be counted as an event in the exposed group. This artificially deflates the event rate in the GLP-1 group.
findings.direction: This bias systematically reduces the apparent risk in the exposed group, pushing the odds ratio below 1.0. The observed OR of ~0.7 is consistent with the direction of this bias.

Метод оценки: Логистическая регрессия, оценка через odds ratio. Time-to-event анализ не проводился.

findings.title: Confounding by Weight Loss (Mediation)
findings.mechanism: GLP-1 agonists cause weight loss, and weight loss itself is a known factor for reducing breast cancer risk. The study matched on 'maximum BMI', not on BMI at baseline or its change over time. The observed protective effect may not be from the drug's direct pharmacology, but rather from the weight loss it induces. The control group, while matched on a historical maximum BMI, likely did not experience the same degree of weight loss during the study period.
findings.direction: This would make the GLP-1 group appear to have a lower risk of breast cancer, as they are more likely to have lost weight. This pushes the odds ratio below 1.0.

findings.title: Selection Bias (Confounding by Contraindication)
findings.mechanism: The study did not match on prior history of breast cancer. Clinicians may be less likely to prescribe a newer class of drugs to patients with a personal or strong family history of cancer. This would systematically place patients with a lower baseline cancer risk into the GLP-1 group.
findings.direction: This selection process would lead to a lower incidence of cancer in the GLP-1 group, creating a spurious association of protection and pushing the odds ratio below 1.0.

findings.title: Healthy User Bias
findings.mechanism: Patients who are prescribed and take a GLP-1 agonist for obesity or diabetes may be more health-conscious and proactive about their health in general (e.g., diet, exercise, adherence to screening) than the matched control group. These unmeasured healthy behaviors are also associated with a lower risk of cancer.
findings.direction: The unmeasured healthier lifestyle in the GLP-1 group would lead to a lower cancer incidence, biasing the result towards a protective effect (OR < 1.0).
evidence: The study is an observational design based on EHR data, which typically lacks detailed lifestyle information.

findings.title: Immortal Time Bias
findings.mechanism: The study uses logistic regression instead of a time-to-event analysis. Patients in the GLP-1 group must, by definition, survive without a breast cancer diagnosis long enough to receive a prescription. This period of event-free survival is 'immortal time' that is incorrectly credited to the exposure group. The control group has no such requirement, creating a built-in survival advantage for the GLP-1 group.
findings.direction: Biases the result towards a protective effect (OR < 1.0). The design guarantees a period of survival for the exposed group that is not guaranteed for the control group. This artifactually lowers the event rate in the GLP-1 arm, which is consistent with the observed OR of 0.695.

findings.title: Protopathic Bias (Reverse Causation)
findings.mechanism: The outcome (undiagnosed breast cancer) may have influenced the prescription of the exposure (GLP-1 agonist). For example, early-stage cancer can cause metabolic changes or unexplained weight loss, which could lead a physician to avoid prescribing a weight-loss medication. This would systematically remove patients with incipient cancer from the GLP-1 group, making the drug appear protective.
findings.direction: Biases the result towards a protective effect (OR < 1.0). If patients with early, undiagnosed cancer are less likely to receive a GLP-1 prescription, the GLP-1 group will be artificially healthier with respect to cancer risk at baseline. This matches the observed protective association.

findings.title: Residual Confounding due to Failed Matching
findings.mechanism: Despite 1:1 matching, the groups remain severely imbalanced on critical prognostic factors. The GLP-1 group has a higher prevalence of personal history of breast cancer and a much higher burden of general comorbidity. Since these factors increase cancer risk, the groups are not comparable.
findings.direction: This specific confounding biases the result towards a harmful effect (OR > 1.0). The GLP-1 group is sicker (Charlson ≥ 5: 19.7% vs 10.4%) and has more prior cancer history (7.8% vs 5.9%), both of which should increase their observed cancer rate. The fact that the study found a protective effect *despite* these imbalances suggests that other biases (like immortal time and protopathic bias) are extremely strong and are overwhelming this effect.

Индекс Charlson ≥ 5 (Коморбидность): GLP-1 19.7% против контроль 10.4%

findings.title: Biased Matching on a Dynamic Variable
findings.mechanism: The study matched patients on their *maximum* BMI. GLP-1 agonists cause weight loss. Therefore, the study is comparing a group (GLP-1) whose current BMI is likely lower than their maximum, to a group (control) whose current and maximum BMI may be the same. Since obesity is a risk factor for breast cancer, this compares people with different current risk profiles, not similar ones.
findings.direction: Biases the result towards a protective effect (OR < 1.0). The GLP-1 patient, having lost weight, likely has a lower current BMI and thus lower obesity-related cancer risk than the control patient with whom they were matched on *maximum* BMI. This creates a spurious protective association.
